Definition: from a derivative of G4621; grained, i.e. fatted:--fatling.
BiblicalUsage: Sitistos means fatted, fed on grain, and it appears once, in the parable of the wedding feast, where the king sends his servants to tell the bidden guests that his oxen and his fatlings are killed and all things are ready.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the king's fatlings say the feast is real, because a wedding with nothing ready is no wedding at all.
